class temporal.modules.losses.loss_functions.MQLoss(quantiles: list, reduction: str = 'mean', use_crps: bool = False)[source]¶

Bases: torch.nn.Module

Computes the Multi-Quantile Loss (MQL) for probabilistic forecasting.

This loss function computes the average pinball loss over a set of specified quantiles. It is a common metric for evaluating the accuracy of quantile forecasts.

quantiles¶

The quantiles to be evaluated.

Type:

torch.Tensor

reduction[source]¶

The reduction method to apply to the final loss.

Type:

str

use_crps[source]¶

If True, adds a penalty term to approximate the CRPS.

Type:

bool

reduction = 'mean'[source]¶
use_crps = False[source]¶
forward(preds: torch.Tensor, target: torch.Tensor) → torch.Tensor[source]¶

Calculates the Multi-Quantile Loss.

Parameters:

  • preds (torch.Tensor) – The predicted quantiles, shape (B, T, Q).

  • target (torch.Tensor) – The ground truth values, shape (B, T).

Returns:

The computed loss, as a scalar or a tensor depending on the reduction method.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

class temporal.modules.losses.loss_functions.WeightedQuantileLoss(quantiles: tuple = (0.1, 0.5, 0.9), epsilon: float = 1e-08, reduction: str = 'mean')[source]¶

Bases: torch.nn.Module

Computes the Weighted Quantile Loss (wQL).

wQL is a variant of the quantile loss that is normalized by the sum of the absolute target values. This can be useful for stabilizing training when the target values have a large dynamic range.

quantiles¶

The quantiles to be evaluated.

Type:

torch.Tensor

epsilon[source]¶

A small constant to prevent division by zero.

Type:

float

reduction[source]¶

The reduction method.

Type:

str

class temporal.modules.losses.loss_functions.QuantileLoss(quantile: float, reduction: str = 'mean')[source]¶

Bases: torch.nn.Module

Computes the Quantile Loss (also known as Pinball Loss).

This loss function is used for quantile regression. It asymmetrically penalizes over- and under-prediction to encourage the model to output a specific quantile of the target distribution.

quantile[source]¶

The target quantile, between 0 and 1.

Type:

float

reduction[source]¶

The reduction method.

Type:

str

quantile[source]¶
reduction = 'mean'[source]¶
forward(predictions: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor) → torch.Tensor[source]¶

Calculates the Quantile Loss.

class temporal.modules.losses.loss_functions.KernelEnergyLoss(reduction: str = 'mean')[source]¶

Bases: torch.nn.Module

Computes a kernel-based energy distance loss for probabilistic forecasts.

This loss function is a proper scoring rule that encourages the distribution of predicted samples to match the distribution of the true data. It is based on the energy distance between the two distributions.

reduction = 'mean'[source]¶
forward(preds: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor) → torch.Tensor[source]¶

Calculates the kernel-based energy loss.

Parameters:

  • preds (torch.Tensor) – A tensor of predicted samples, shape (B, T, N).

  • targets (torch.Tensor) – The ground truth values, shape (B, T).

Returns:

The computed loss.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

class temporal.modules.losses.loss_functions.SpectralLoss(reduction: str = 'mean')[source]¶

Bases: torch.nn.Module

Computes a loss in the frequency domain.

This loss function calculates the L2 distance between the Fast Fourier Transforms (FFTs) of the predictions and the targets. It encourages the model to match the frequency components of the target sequence.

reduction = 'mean'[source]¶
forward(preds: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor) → torch.Tensor[source]¶

Calculates the spectral loss.

class temporal.modules.losses.loss_functions.FastSoftDTWLoss(gamma: float = 1.0, reduction: str = 'mean')[source]¶

Bases: torch.nn.Module

Computes a differentiable approximation of Dynamic Time Warping (DTW).

Soft-DTW is a differentiable loss function that measures the alignment between two time series. It can be useful for tasks where the sequences might be out of phase.

gamma[source]¶

The smoothing parameter. A lower gamma makes the loss closer to the non-differentiable DTW.

Type:

float

gamma = 1.0[source]¶
reduction = 'mean'[source]¶
forward(preds: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor) → torch.Tensor[source]¶

Calculates the Soft-DTW loss.

class temporal.modules.losses.loss_functions.SpreadPenalty(penalty_type: str = 'log', epsilon: float = 0.001, reduction: str = 'mean', target_spread: float = 0.0)[source]¶

Bases: torch.nn.Module

Computes a penalty on the spread of predicted quantiles.

This module is used to regularize the uncertainty of a probabilistic forecast. It can penalize excessively wide or narrow quantile ranges.

class temporal.modules.losses.loss_functions.MixtureLoss(reduction='mean', min_df=2.0, fixed_sigma=0.001)[source]¶

Bases: torch.nn.Module

Computes the Negative Log-Likelihood for a Mixture Density Network.

This loss function is designed to work with the output of a MixtureOutputHead. It calculates the likelihood of the target values under a mixture of probability distributions, whose parameters are predicted by the model.

min_df[source]¶

The minimum degrees of freedom for a Student’s T distribution.

Type:

float

fixed_sigma[source]¶

The fixed standard deviation for a Normal distribution if its sigma is not predicted.

Type:

float

reduction = 'mean'[source]¶
min_df = 2.0[source]¶
fixed_sigma = 0.001[source]¶
forward(preds: dict, targets: torch.Tensor, loss_mask: torch.Tensor = None)[source]¶

Calculates the mixture loss.

Parameters:

  • preds (dict) – A dictionary of predicted parameters from a MixtureOutputHead.

  • targets (torch.Tensor) – The ground truth values.

  • loss_mask (Optional[torch.Tensor]) – An optional mask for the loss.

Returns:

The final computed loss.

Return type:

torch.Tensor
